facts.design_impact: `payloadData` is the way to read binary tickets such as Deutsche Bahn UIC 918.3 Aztec codes. Any deployment target of iOS 17 or later removes the need for a fallback. Never round-trip binary payloads through String.

facts.claim: `CIBarcodeDescriptor` subclasses are `CIQRCodeDescriptor`, `CIAztecCodeDescriptor`, `CIPDF417CodeDescriptor` and `CIDataMatrixCodeDescriptor`. Each has `errorCorrectedPayload: Data`, and that value is codewords, not decoded bytes. For QR it is the 8-bit codewords right after 'bitstream to codeword conversion' (ISO 18004). For Aztec it is the 6/8/10/12-bit data codewords with inserted dummy bits that you must strip (ISO 24778). For PDF417 it is 16-bit codewords 0…928, with the first one giving the count (ISO 15438). For Data Matrix it is the de-interleaved data-encodation bits. The extra properties are `symbolVersion`, `maskPattern`, `errorCorrectionLevel`, `isCompact`, `layerCount`, `dataCodewordCount`, `rowCount` and `columnCount`.
facts.design_impact: Before iOS 17, getting raw bytes meant writing your own high-level decoder per symbology. That is a strong reason not to support iOS 16. Keep the descriptor only for debugging or for re-rendering the identical symbol.

facts.claim: Swift-native Vision `DetectBarcodesRequest` (struct, Sendable) is available from iOS 18.0. API: `init(_ revision: DetectBarcodesRequest.Revision?)` (the only revision is `.revision4`), `symbologies: [BarcodeSymbology]`, `supportedSymbologies` (documented as potentially expensive), `coalescesCompositeSymbologies`, and `perform(on: CGImage | URL | Data | CVPixelBuffer | CMSampleBuffer | CIImage, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws`. `BarcodeSymbology` is a CaseIterable, Codable, Sendable enum with the same case names as `VNBarcodeSymbology`.
facts.design_impact: Use this as the still-image and PDF-page decoder. It's async and Sendable, so it fits Swift 6 strict concurrency.

facts.claim: `BarcodeObservation` (iOS 18, Sendable, Codable) has `payloadString` (not `payloadStringValue`), `payloadData: Data?`, `supplementalPayloadString`, `supplementalPayloadData`, `supplementalCompositeType`, `symbology: BarcodeSymbology`, `isGS1DataCarrier`, `isColorInverted` and `boundingRegion`, plus `init(_ observation: VNBarcodeObservation)`. It has no `barcodeDescriptor`.
facts.design_impact: Normalize both sources into one DTO: the VisionKit live path gives a VNBarcodeObservation, the still-image path gives a BarcodeObservation. `BarcodeObservation(vnObservation)` can do the conversion. Code that needs the CIBarcodeDescriptor must use the VN API.

facts.claim: `ImageRequestHandler` (iOS 18) is a final, Sendable class. It has inits for CGImage, URL, Data, CIImage, CVPixelBuffer and CMSampleBuffer, each with `orientation:`. It offers `perform<each T>(repeat each T) async throws -> (repeat (each T).Result)` and `performAll(_:)`. The legacy `VNImageRequestHandler.perform(_ requests: [VNRequest]) throws` is synchronous and returns only after every request finishes. Neither `VNImageRequestHandler` nor `VNRequest` is Sendable.
facts.design_impact: One pass works: `let (codes, text) = try await ImageRequestHandler(cgImage, orientation: o).perform(DetectBarcodesRequest(), RecognizeTextRequest())`. Legacy VN code has to run inside a single non-main isolation domain.

facts.claim: `RecognizeTextRequest` (iOS 18, Sendable) has `recognitionLanguages: [Locale.Language]`, `supportedRecognitionLanguages`, `automaticallyDetectsLanguage`, `usesLanguageCorrection`, `customWords`, `minimumTextHeightFraction` and `recognitionLevel` (`.accurate` or `.fast`). The only revision is `.revision3`. It returns `RecognizedTextObservation`, with `transcript`, `topCandidates(_:)`, `boundingRegion` and `recognitionLanguages`. The legacy `VNRecognizeTextRequest` (iOS 13) uses `recognitionLanguages: [String]` and `supportedRecognitionLanguages() throws`; Revision3 is iOS 16, and Revisions 1 and 2 are deprecated.
facts.design_impact: For German, set `recognitionLanguages = [Locale.Language(identifier: "de-DE"), Locale.Language(identifier: "en-US")]` and check at runtime that they appear in `supportedRecognitionLanguages`. I didn't verify the German list for Vision itself; DataScanner's article does use "de-DE". VN page: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/vnrecognizetextrequest

facts.claim: `RecognizeDocumentsRequest` (iOS 26.0) returns `DocumentObservation`. Its `document: DocumentObservation.Container` exposes `text`, `paragraphs`, `title`, `tables`, `lists` and `barcodes: [BarcodeObservation]`. `Container.Text` has `transcript`, `lines`, `words` and `detectedData: [DataDetectorMatch]`, where each match has `match: DataDetector.Match`. Configuration: `barcodeDetectionOptions` (`enabled`, `symbologies`, `coalesceCompositeSymbologies`) and `textRecognitionOptions` (`recognitionLanguages`, `automaticallyDetectLanguage`, `useLanguageCorrection`, `customWords`, `maximumCandidateCount`, `minimumTextHeightFraction`).
facts.design_impact: On iOS 26 and later, a single request returns the barcodes, structured text and detected dates or flight numbers for a ticket photo or PDF page, which suits the field auto-suggestion feature. Watch out: the property names differ from RecognizeTextRequest (`automaticallyDetectLanguage` vs `automaticallyDetectsLanguage`, `useLanguageCorrection` vs `usesLanguageCorrection`) and from DetectBarcodesRequest (`coalesceCompositeSymbologies` vs `coalescesCompositeSymbologies`). Data detector page: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/documentobservation/container/datadetectormatch

facts.claim: The Swift DataDetection API is iOS 26.0: `StringProtocol.dataDetectorMatches(_ types: DataDetector.MatchType = .all, options: DataDetector.Options = .init()) -> some AsyncSequence<DataDetector.Match, Never>`. Match types: `.calendarEvent`, `.flightNumber`, `.moneyAmount`, `.postalAddress`, `.link`, `.emailAddress`, `.phoneNumber`, `.measurement`, `.shipmentTrackingNumber`, `.paymentIdentifier` and `.all`. A match has `details` (for example `.calendarEvent(CalendarEvent)` with `startDate`, `endDate`, `allDay`, `startTimeZone` and `endTimeZone`) and `range`. Options: `documentDate`, `documentLanguageCode`, `documentRegion` and `documentTimeZone`. The legacy `NSDataDetector` (iOS 4) takes `NSTextCheckingResult.CheckingType.date`; Apple says not to use it for validation, because it drops uncertain matches.
facts.design_impact: Suggest relevantDate, expiry and flight number from OCR text. Set the options to `documentLanguageCode` .german, `documentRegion` .germany and `documentTimeZone` Europe/Berlin so German formats like dd.MM.yyyy parse correctly. Everything is a suggestion that the user confirms. NSDataDetector page: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsdatadetector

facts.claim: `PhotosPicker` (PhotosUI, iOS 16) is a `@MainActor @preconcurrency struct`. Inits include `init(selection: Binding<PhotosPickerItem?>, matching: PHPickerFilter?, preferredItemEncoding:, label:)` and a multi-selection version with `maxSelectionCount`. `PhotosPickerItem` is Sendable and Transferable, with `loadTransferable(type:) async throws -> sending T?`. SwiftUI `Image` loads only PNG and JPEG through Transferable. The picker runs out of process, so it needs no photo-library authorization.
facts.design_impact: Use `matching: .images` (screenshots allowed) and `loadTransferable(type: Data.self)`; Data conforms to Transferable. Then decode with `UIImage(data:)` or CGImageSource so HEIC and EXIF orientation work. Don't add NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription. Privacy page: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/photokit/delivering-an-enhanced-privacy-experience-in-your-photos-app

facts.claim: SwiftUI `.fileImporter(isPresented:allowedContentTypes:allowsMultipleSelection:onCompletion:)` is iOS 14; its result is `Result<[URL], Error>`. The URLs are security-scoped: call `startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()` before reading and `stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource()` afterwards.
facts.design_impact: Use `allowedContentTypes: [.pdf, .image]`. Copy the file into the app sandbox right away, while access is open.

facts.claim: PDFKit: `PDFDocument(url:)` and `PDFDocument(data:)` are failable inits. `pageCount` gives the page count; `page(at:)` is zero-based and raises an exception when out of bounds. `PDFPage.bounds(for: .mediaBox)` is in page space, so rotation may need a transform. `PDFPage.thumbnail(of: CGSize, for: PDFDisplayBox) -> UIImage` and `draw(with: PDFDisplayBox, to: CGContext)` are iOS 11. `UIGraphicsImageRenderer(size:format:)` with `UIGraphicsImageRendererFormat.scale` and `.opaque` produces a UIImage via `image(actions:)`.
facts.design_impact: Render each page to a bitmap at about 300 dpi (scale ≈ 300/72), with a white background and a cap on pixel size. Then run DetectBarcodesRequest. Check `index < pageCount` before calling `page(at:)`. Page: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/pdfkit/pdfpage/draw(with:to:)

facts.claim: Share Extension Info.plist: `NSExtension` > `NSExtensionPointIdentifier` = `com.apple.share-services`; `NSExtensionAttributes` > `NSExtensionActivationRule`. The rule is either a dictionary (keys such as `NSExtensionActivationSupportsImageWithMaxCount`, `NSExtensionActivationSupportsFileWithMaxCount`, `NSExtensionActivationSupportsWebURLWithMaxCount`, `NSExtensionActivationSupportsAttachmentsWithMinCount`/`MaxCount`) or a SUBQUERY predicate string. Apple's single-PDF example is `SUBQUERY(extensionItems, $extensionItem, SUBQUERY($extensionItem.attachments, $attachment, ANY $attachment.registeredTypeIdentifiers UTI-CONFORMS-TO "com.adobe.pdf").@count == $extensionItem.attachments.@count).@count == 1`. If any extension contains `TRUEPREDICATE`, App Review rejects the app.
facts.design_impact: Use a predicate that accepts com.adobe.pdf OR public.image, so Mail and Safari PDFs and images trigger the extension. Key reference: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/nsextension/nsextensionattributes/nsextensionactivationrule

facts.claim: An app extension and its containing app can't reach each other's containers. To share data they need an App Group: entitlement `com.apple.security.application-groups`, and `UserDefaults(suiteName:)` or a shared container with coordinated access. `NSExtensionContext.open(_:)` is supported on iOS only by the Today and iMessage extension points, so a Share extension cannot officially launch its containing app.
facts.design_impact: The share extension should copy the PDF or image into an App Group 'inbox' folder and tell the user it will appear in QRCode2Wallet. The main app picks up the inbox items on launch or when it becomes active. Load attachments with `NSItemProvider.loadFileRepresentation(for: .pdf, openInPlace: false)` or `loadDataRepresentation(for:)` (iOS 16, @Sendable handlers).

facts.claim: `PKPass.init(data: Data) throws` expects a signed pass. Signature problems throw `PKPassKitError.Code.invalidSignature` and bad data throws `.invalidDataError`. The other codes are `.unsupportedVersionError`, `.notEntitledError` and `.unknownError`. `PKPass` is not Sendable.
facts.design_impact: Download the .pkpass as `Data`, which is Sendable, then build the PKPass on the MainActor. Map invalidSignature to a 'backend signing broken' alert and telemetry event.

facts.claim: `PKPassLibrary` is not thread-safe; use each instance on a single thread. `isPassLibraryAvailable()` does not tell you whether passes can be added; use `PKAddPassesViewController.canAddPasses()` (iOS 8) for that. `passes()` returns only the passes the app's entitlements allow. `containsPass(_:)` works without read entitlements. `replacePass(with:) -> Bool` replaces only an existing pass with the same passTypeIdentifier and serialNumber. `addPasses(_:withCompletionHandler:)` (iOS 7) has an async form, `addPasses(_:) async -> PKPassLibraryAddPassesStatus`, returning `.didAddPasses`, `.shouldReviewPasses` (you must then present PKAddPassesViewController) or `.didCancelAddPasses`.
facts.design_impact: Keep one PKPassLibrary on the MainActor. Use `containsPass` to show an 'In Wallet' badge. A SwiftUI flow can call `await library.addPasses([pass])` and only present a VC on `.shouldReviewPasses`.

facts.claim: Adding a pass needs no entitlement, because the user approves it explicitly. Reading, updating and deleting passes need the Pass Type IDs entitlement `com.apple.developer.pass-type-identifiers`, an array of pass type identifiers added through the Wallet capability; `$(TeamIdentifierPrefix)*` means all of the team's passes.
facts.design_impact: V1 can ship without the Wallet capability. To edit or regenerate passes in place (`pass(withPassTypeIdentifier:serialNumber:)`, `replacePass`, `removePass`), enable Wallet with the backend's own Pass Type ID, since passes are signed by the backend under our team. Entitlement page: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/entitlements/com.apple.developer.pass-type-identifiers

facts.claim: New in iOS 26.0: `PKPassLibrary.Capability.backgroundAddPasses`, `requestAuthorization(for:) async -> PKPassLibrary.AuthorizationStatus` and `authorizationStatus(for:)`. Status values are `.authorized`, `.denied`, `.notDetermined` and `.restricted`. Once authorized, `addPasses` adds passes without a confirmation prompt and the system shows a notification instead. The permission prompt appears once and the user can change it in Settings. The app must be installed and running.
facts.design_impact: This is optional. In a converter app the user should see the generated pass before it lands in Wallet, so the default should still go through review. Possible use: silent regeneration. Flow description: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/walletpasses/distributing-and-updating-a-pass

facts.claim: New in iOS 27.0: `PKPassLibrary.addPasses(data: [Data]) async -> PKPassLibraryAddPassesStatus`, `addPasses(fromArchiveData:)`, `addPasses(fromArchiveAt:)`, and `PKAddPassesViewController.init?(passesData: [Data])`, `init?(passesArchiveData:)` and `init?(passesArchiveAt:)`.
facts.design_impact: These let you hand raw .pkpass bytes straight to Wallet without building a PKPass. Use them only behind `if #available(iOS 27, *)`; the iOS 26 baseline uses `PKPass(data:)`.

facts.claim: `PKAddPassesViewController` (iOS 6) has `init?(pass:)`, `init?(passes:)` and `delegate: PKAddPassesViewControllerDelegate`, whose callback is `addPassesViewControllerDidFinish(_:)`. SwiftUI `AddPassToWalletButton` (PassKit, iOS 16, not available on visionOS) is `@MainActor @preconcurrency struct AddPassToWalletButton<Fallback: View>` with `init(_ passes: [PKPass], onCompletion: @escaping (Bool) -> Void)`, a `fallback:` variant and `init(action: @escaping () -> Void)`. The style modifier is `.addPassToWalletButtonStyle(_:)` (`.black`, `.blackOutline`). The UIKit equivalent is `PKAddPassButton(addPassButtonStyle:)` (iOS 9).
facts.design_impact: Once the PKPass exists, use `AddPassToWalletButton([pass]) { added in ... }`. If you need to download or sign first, use `init(action:)` and then call `addPasses`. Wrap PKAddPassesViewController in UIViewControllerRepresentable only for the `.shouldReviewPasses` case.

facts.claim: The Wallet pass `barcodes[]` object has the keys `format`, `message`, `messageEncoding` (an IANA charset such as "iso-8859-1") and an optional `altText`. Allowed `format` values: PKBarcodeFormatQR, PKBarcodeFormatPDF417, PKBarcodeFormatAztec, PKBarcodeFormatCode128, PKBarcodeFormatCode39, PKBarcodeFormatCodabar, PKBarcodeFormatEAN13 and PKBarcodeFormatI2of5. From iOS 27 you can list several barcodes as fallbacks: EAN-13 renders on iOS 27 and later, QR on older versions.
facts.design_impact: The client needs a symbology-compatibility table. Data Matrix, EAN-8, UPC-E, ITF-14, Code 93, GS1 DataBar, microQR and microPDF417 can't be rendered by Wallet as-is. Send the raw bytes (base64) plus the symbology to the backend, and let it choose the format plus a fallback.

facts.claim: The MIME type for a .pkpass is application/vnd.apple.pkpass. A .pkpasses bundle (a zip of .pkpass files) uses application/vnd.apple.pkpasses and is limited to 10 passes or 150 MB.
facts.design_impact: The client should check the `Content-Type` and the 200 status before calling `PKPass(data:)`. Bundle limits: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/walletpasses/distributing-and-updating-a-pass

facts.claim: SwiftData (iOS 17): the `@Model` macro adds Observable and PersistentModel conformances; the current SDK declaration also lists Sendable. `Schema.Attribute.Option.externalStorage` is iOS 17 and `#Unique<T>([\.keyPath], ...)` is iOS 18. `ModelConfiguration(_:schema:isStoredInMemoryOnly:allowsSave:groupContainer:cloudKitDatabase:)` accepts `.automatic`, `.identifier("group...")` or `.none`. `.modelContainer(for:inMemory:isAutosaveEnabled:isUndoEnabled:onSetup:)` is a `@MainActor` view modifier. `@ModelActor` gives background contexts, and `PersistentIdentifier` is Sendable and Codable.
facts.design_impact: Model: `@Model final class PassRecord { #Unique<PassRecord>([\.serialNumber]); var serialNumber: String; var passTypeIdentifier: String; var symbology: String; @Attribute(.externalStorage) var payload: Data; @Attribute(.externalStorage) var pkpassData: Data?; @Attribute(.externalStorage) var sourceImage: Data?; var createdAt: Date }`. Pass PersistentIdentifier across actors, not model objects. Macro and attribute pages: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftdata/model() and https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftdata/unique(_:)

facts.claim: URLSession async APIs (iOS 15): `data(for: URLRequest, delegate:) async throws -> (Data, URLResponse)`, `upload(for: URLRequest, from: Data, delegate:) async throws -> (Data, URLResponse)` and `download(for: URLRequest, delegate:) async throws -> (URL, URLResponse)`.
facts.design_impact: POST the JSON with `upload(for:from:)` and `Content-Type: application/json`, receiving the .pkpass bytes in the response, or use a separate GET with `data(for:)`. Cast the response to HTTPURLResponse and check the status. Passes are small, so `data(for:)` is enough.

facts.claim: `DCAppAttestService.shared` (iOS 14) has `isSupported` plus async APIs: `generateKey() async throws -> String` (key identifier), `attestKey(_ keyId: String, clientDataHash: Data) async throws -> Data` (attestation object) and `generateAssertion(_ keyId: String, clientDataHash: Data) async throws -> Data`. `clientDataHash` is the SHA256 of data that includes a one-time server challenge of at least 16 bytes. On `serverUnavailable`, retry with the same key and hash; on any other error, discard the key. Keys survive app updates but not reinstall, device migration or backup restore. Apple recommends one key per user account per device. `DCError.Code` values: `featureUnsupported`, `invalidInput`, `invalidKey`, `serverUnavailable` and `unknownSystemFailure`.
facts.design_impact: Client flow: GET /attest/challenge → `generateKey` → `attestKey(keyId, SHA256(challenge))` → POST {keyId, attestation(base64), challenge} → store keyId in the Keychain. Then for each signing request: GET /challenge → `clientData = JSON(request + challenge)` → `generateAssertion(keyId, SHA256(clientData))` → send the assertion with the request. On `invalidKey`, re-attest.

facts.claim: `isSupported` is false on Mac, including Mac Catalyst and iOS apps running on Apple silicon. `generateKey` fails in most app extensions even when `isSupported` is true. The isSupported page says only watchOS extensions (watchOS 9 and later) are supported; the integrity article says Action, extensible SSO and watchOS extensions are. Share extensions are unsupported according to both.
facts.design_impact: The Share extension can't attest, so backend calls that require App Attest have to come from the main app (hence the inbox design). The server needs a policy for devices that can't attest: Simulator, Mac and older devices. Whether Action extensions are supported is contradictory in Apple's docs; treat it as unverified.

facts.claim: App Attest entitlement: `com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment`, with value `development` or `production`. Builds distributed through TestFlight or the App Store ignore it and use production. Sandbox keys and production keys don't work in each other's environment. An App ID registered on the developer portal is required.
facts.design_impact: Put it in the app's entitlements, generated by XcodeGen. The backend has to verify against the matching environment, recognizable from the AAGUID in the attestation.

facts.claim: Swift 6.2 concurrency proposals: SE-0466 (Implemented in Swift 6.2) adds default `@MainActor` isolation inference per module. SE-0461 (Implemented in Swift 6.2, feature flag `NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault`) makes nonisolated async functions run on the caller's actor unless marked `@concurrent`. Xcode build settings: `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION` (MainActor or nonisolated); `SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY`, which turns on DisableOutwardActorInference, GlobalActorIsolatedTypesUsability, InferIsolatedConformances, InferSendableFromCaptures and NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault; and `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY`, which is always 'complete' in Swift 6 mode and reports errors.
facts.design_impact: With these settings, a plain `func decode(_:) async` called from a SwiftUI view runs on the main thread. CPU-heavy steps (PDF rasterizing, VN* synchronous perform, image decoding) must be `@concurrent` or live on a dedicated actor. Proposals: https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolution/blob/main/proposals/0466-control-default-actor-isolation.md and https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolution/blob/main/proposals/0461-async-function-isolation.md

facts.claim: Xcode 26 project templates reportedly default to `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor` for new projects, while existing projects stay nonisolated. Sources disagree on whether Approachable Concurrency is also enabled by default.
facts.design_impact: XcodeGen doesn't apply Xcode's new-project template defaults, so set both settings explicitly in project.yml to get predictable behaviour.

facts.claim: Sendable status in the current SDK docs. Sendable: UIImage, CGImage, Data, PhotosPickerItem, VNBarcodeSymbology, and all Swift-native Vision requests and observations (DetectBarcodesRequest, BarcodeObservation, RecognizeTextRequest, RecognizeDocumentsRequest, DocumentObservation, ImageRequestHandler), as well as PKAddPassesViewController and AddPassToWalletButton. Not Sendable: VNImageRequestHandler, VNRequest, VNBarcodeObservation (an NSObject without Sendable), RecognizedItem / RecognizedItem.Barcode / RecognizedItem.Text, PKPass and PKPassLibrary. `UIViewControllerRepresentable` is `@MainActor @preconcurrency`.
facts.design_impact: Only Data, CGImage, UIImage and Codable DTOs should cross actor boundaries. Keep VisionKit items, PKPass, PKPassLibrary and ModelContext on the MainActor. UIImage: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiimage

facts.claim: Observation's `@Observable` macro is iOS 17.
facts.design_impact: Use `@Observable` view models instead of ObservableObject. Any deployment target of iOS 17 or later allows it.

facts.claim: `INFOPLIST_KEY_NSCameraUsageDescription` is a real Xcode build setting, applied when `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE` is enabled. The build system merges an explicit INFOPLIST_FILE with the values it generates.
facts.design_impact: With XcodeGen, either generate the full Info.plist via `info: properties:` or use INFOPLIST_KEY_* settings, and pick one. A target-level `info:` block is the more readable choice in YAML.

facts.claim: XcodeGen: the latest released version is 2.46.0 according to CHANGELOG.md. `options.projectFormat` values go up to `xcode16_3` (default `xcode16_0`). Target keys: `type` (`application`, `app-extension`, `bundle.unit-test`, …), `platform`, `deploymentTarget`, `sources`, `settings`, `dependencies`, `info: {path, properties}` (writes Info.plist and sets INFOPLIST_FILE; generates CFBundleIdentifier, CFBundleVersion and similar), `entitlements: {path, properties}` (writes .entitlements and sets CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS) and `scheme: {testTargets, gatherCoverageData}`. TEST_HOST is set automatically for unit tests that depend on an app. A `target:` dependency embeds by default in application targets. Code signing is configured only through DEVELOPMENT_TEAM and CODE_SIGN_STYLE. XcodeGen doesn't abstract capabilities; you add entitlements and frameworks yourself.
facts.design_impact: Generate the .xcodeproj in CI with `xcodegen generate` and don't commit it. Capabilities such as Wallet, App Groups and App Attest go in as `entitlements.properties`, and must also be enabled on the App ID in the developer portal. Changelog and FAQ: https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md and https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen/blob/master/Docs/FAQ.md

facts.claim: VisionKit also includes `VNDocumentCameraViewController` (paper document scanning UI) and `ImageAnalyzer`/`ImageAnalysisInteraction` (Live Text on still images).
facts.design_impact: Optionally, offer 'scan paper ticket' through VNDocumentCameraViewController: it produces perspective-corrected pages that can go to DetectBarcodesRequest when a live scan fails on a crumpled printout.

recommendations.decision: Set the minimum deployment target to iOS 26.0, build with Xcode 27 (iOS 27 SDK), and put iOS 27 APIs behind `if #available(iOS 27, *)`. If market data later demands it, the fallback floor is iOS 18.0, never lower.
recommendations.rationale: iOS 17 is the absolute minimum because it adds `VNBarcodeObservation.payloadData` (raw bytes for binary UIC 918.3 tickets; before that you need a custom codeword decoder), SwiftData and `@Observable`. iOS 18 adds the Sendable Swift Vision API (DetectBarcodesRequest, BarcodeObservation.payloadData, RecognizeTextRequest, ImageRequestHandler) and SwiftData `#Unique`. iOS 26 adds RecognizeDocumentsRequest (barcodes, text and data detection in one pass), the Swift DataDetector API and PassKit backgroundAddPasses. On reach: 79% of all iPhones ran iOS 26 in June 2026, and iOS 26 and 27 support the same devices (iPhone 11 and later). The only devices you give up are iPhone XS and XR plus people who haven't updated. Choosing iOS 26 also avoids maintaining two pipelines (VN and Swift Vision) under Swift 6 strict concurrency.

recommendations.decision: Swift settings in project.yml: `SWIFT_VERSION: 6.0`, `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION: MainActor`, `SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY: YES`. Mark CPU-heavy functions `@concurrent nonisolated` (PDF rasterizing, image decoding, any VN* synchronous perform), or put them in an `actor ImagePipeline`.
recommendations.rationale: With MainActor-by-default and NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault, unannotated async helpers run on the main thread and would freeze the UI during PDF rendering or decoding. Swift 6 mode makes every data-race diagnostic an error. Setting these explicitly makes XcodeGen output behave the same as Xcode 26/27 templates.

recommendations.decision: Live scan: write `struct ScannerView: UIViewControllerRepresentable` that builds `DataScannerViewController(recognizedDataTypes: [.barcode(symbologies: [.qr, .aztec, .pdf417, .dataMatrix, .code128, .code39, .code93, .ean13, .ean8, .upce, .itf14, .i2of5, .codabar, .gs1DataBar, .gs1DataBarExpanded, .microQR, .microPDF417])], qualityLevel: .accurate, recognizesMultipleItems: false, isHighFrameRateTrackingEnabled: false, isPinchToZoomEnabled: true, isGuidanceEnabled: true, isHighlightingEnabled: true)`. The Coordinator is an `NSObject, DataScannerViewControllerDelegate`, main-actor isolated. Call `startScanning()` after camera access is granted (catch `ScanningUnavailable`) and `stopScanning()` in `dismantleUIViewController(_:coordinator:)`. In `didTapOn` and in `didAdd`/`didUpdate` (after a stability check), map `.barcode(let b)` to `ScannedCode(symbology: b.observation.symbology.rawValue, payload: b.observation.payloadData, text: b.payloadStringValue)`.
recommendations.rationale: Every API above is verified for iOS 16 and later. RecognizedItem and VNBarcodeObservation are not Sendable, so copy them into a Sendable DTO inside the MainActor delegate call. `.accurate` raises the resolution, which dense Aztec and PDF417 ticket codes need. Show the scanner only when `isSupported && isAvailable`; otherwise open the import UI.

recommendations.decision: Still images, screenshots and PDF pages: `@concurrent func detect(cgImage: CGImage, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation) async throws -> [ScannedCode]`, which runs `ImageRequestHandler(cgImage, orientation:).perform(DetectBarcodesRequest(.revision4), RecognizeDocumentsRequest())`. Configure `symbologies` explicitly. Read `payloadData` first. If `payloadString` is nil, or doesn't round-trip to the same bytes in UTF-8 or ISO-8859-1, mark the code `isBinary`. Send `payload` to the backend as base64 together with the symbology.
recommendations.rationale: Deutsche Bahn and UIC 918.3 Aztec codes are binary, and turning them into a String can corrupt them. Only `payloadData` guarantees the bytes. The backend can then encode them for Wallet, for example as an ISO-8859-1 1:1 byte-to-char `message` with `messageEncoding: "iso-8859-1"`; confirm that in the pass-format research.

recommendations.decision: PDF import: open with `PDFDocument(url:)` (or from `Data` for share-extension input) and look at pages 0 to min(pageCount, 5) - 1. For each page, take `bounds(for: .mediaBox)`, scale by s = min(300/72, 4096 / max(width, height)), and render with `UIGraphicsImageRenderer(size: scaled, format: fmt)` where `fmt.scale = 1` and `fmt.opaque = true`. Fill white, flip the CTM, and call `page.draw(with: .mediaBox, to: ctx.cgContext)`. If nothing decodes, try again at 2x or by cropping.
recommendations.rationale: Vector barcodes in PDFs decode better at high resolution, and the pixel cap keeps memory bounded. Share extensions are especially memory-constrained, though the exact limit isn't documented. Apply page rotation (`PDFPage.rotation`) to the transform.

recommendations.decision: Field auto-suggestion: on iOS 26+, use `RecognizeDocumentsRequest` with `textRecognitionOptions.recognitionLanguages = [de-DE, en-US]`, take `document.text.detectedData`, and run `transcript.dataDetectorMatches([.calendarEvent, .flightNumber, .moneyAmount, .postalAddress], options:)` with German language code, Germany region and the Europe/Berlin time zone. Map the results to the pass's relevantDate/expirationDate, organizer name (the largest title text) and member number (the text near the barcode). Always ask the user to confirm.
recommendations.rationale: All of these APIs are verified for iOS 26. The DataDetector Swift API returns typed CalendarEvent start and end dates. NSDataDetector only needs to remain as a legacy fallback, and Apple warns it drops uncertain matches.

recommendations.decision: Import entry points: (1) `PhotosPicker(selection:matching: .images)` loading `Data.self`; (2) `.fileImporter(allowedContentTypes: [.pdf, .image])`, copying into the sandbox while security-scoped access is open; (3) a Share Extension (`com.apple.share-services`, SUBQUERY rule for com.adobe.pdf or public.image, at most 1 attachment) that only writes into the App Group inbox `group.<bundle>.qrcode2wallet/Inbox/` plus a small JSON manifest. The main app imports and processes the inbox on `scenePhase == .active`.
recommendations.rationale: The Share extension can't use App Attest (generateKey fails in extensions) and can't launch its containing app (NSExtensionContext.open is only for Today and iMessage). Keeping the extension thin also keeps it within its memory limits. PhotosPicker needs no photo-library permission.

recommendations.decision: Adding passes: download → check the HTTP 200 status and `application/vnd.apple.pkpass` → `let pass = try PKPass(data:)` on the MainActor → if `PKAddPassesViewController.canAddPasses()`, show `AddPassToWalletButton([pass]) { added in … }`, or call `await library.addPasses([pass])` and present PKAddPassesViewController on `.shouldReviewPasses`. Use `library.containsPass(pass)` for UI state. Enable the Wallet capability with the backend's Pass Type ID (`com.apple.developer.pass-type-identifiers`) so you can call `pass(withPassTypeIdentifier:serialNumber:)` and `replacePass(with:)` for in-place edits. Don't use backgroundAddPasses in v1.
recommendations.rationale: Adding needs no entitlement, but replacing, reading or removing our own passes does. Our passes are signed with our team's Pass Type ID, so the entitlement covers them. The user should see each pass generated from a third-party ticket before it goes into Wallet.

recommendations.decision: Persistence: SwiftData `@Model PassRecord` with `#Unique` on serialNumber and `@Attribute(.externalStorage)` for payload, pkpassData and the source image. Use the default store, not the App Group store, because only the main app writes. Background imports go through a `@ModelActor actor PassStore`, and only `PersistentIdentifier` crosses actors.
recommendations.rationale: This uses the verified iOS 17/18 APIs and avoids two processes writing to one SwiftData store. The Share extension uses a file inbox instead. ModelContext is not Sendable.

recommendations.decision: Networking and attestation: `struct APIClient: Sendable` using `URLSession.shared`. Use `upload(for:from:)` for the JSON (ScannedCode DTO plus pass metadata) and get back either the .pkpass bytes or a pass URL fetched with `data(for:)`. An `actor AttestationManager` stores the keyId in the Keychain, attests once per install and user, and adds an assertion header (base64) on each `/passes` POST, signing SHA256 of the request body plus the server challenge. When `isSupported == false` (Simulator, Mac), the server falls back to stricter rate limits.
recommendations.rationale: Every App Attest async API is iOS 14 and verified. Keys don't survive reinstall or restore, so handle `invalidKey` by re-attesting. On `serverUnavailable`, retry with the same key and hash.

recommendations.decision: Starting project.yml for XcodeGen 2.46: `name: QRCode2Wallet`; `options: {bundleIdPrefix: de.example, deploymentTarget: {iOS: "26.0"}, minimumXcodeGenVersion: "2.46.0", createIntermediateGroups: true}`; `settings: {base: {SWIFT_VERSION: "6.0", SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION: MainActor, SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY: YES, DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: <TEAMID>, CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Automatic, MARKETING_VERSION: "1.0.0", CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION: "1"}}`. Targets: (1) `QRCode2Wallet: {type: application, platform: iOS, sources: [App], info: {path: App/Info.plist, properties: {CFBundleDisplayName: QRCode2Wallet, UILaunchScreen: {}, NSCameraUsageDescription: "QRCode2Wallet nutzt die Kamera, um Barcodes und QR-Codes von Tickets und Kundenkarten zu scannen."}}, entitlements: {path: App/QRCode2Wallet.entitlements, properties: {com.apple.security.application-groups: [group.de.example.qrcode2wallet], com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment: development, com.apple.developer.pass-type-identifiers: ["$(TeamIdentifierPrefix)pass.de.example.qrcode2wallet"]}}, dependencies: [{target: ShareExtension}], scheme: {testTargets: [QRCode2WalletTests], gatherCoverageData: true}}`. (2) `ShareExtension: {type: app-extension, platform: iOS, sources: [ShareExtension], info: {path: ShareExtension/Info.plist, properties: {CFBundleDisplayName: QRCode2Wallet, NSExtension: {NSExtensionPointIdentifier: com.apple.share-services, NSExtensionPrincipalClass: "$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).ShareViewController", NSExtensionAttributes: {NSExtensionActivationRule: "SUBQUERY (extensionItems, $extensionItem, SUBQUERY ($extensionItem.attachments, $attachment, ANY $attachment.registeredTypeIdentifiers UTI-CONFORMS-TO \"com.adobe.pdf\" || ANY $attachment.registeredTypeIdentifiers UTI-CONFORMS-TO \"public.image\").@count == $extensionItem.attachments.@count).@count == 1"}}}}, entitlements: {path: ShareExtension/ShareExtension.entitlements, properties: {com.apple.security.application-groups: [group.de.example.qrcode2wallet]}}}`. (3) `QRCode2WalletTests: {type: bundle.unit-test, platform: iOS, sources: [Tests], dependencies: [{target: QRCode2Wallet}]}`.
recommendations.rationale: Every key used here is documented in ProjectSpec.md: options, settings.base, info, entitlements, dependencies, scheme.testTargets and bundle.unit-test with an automatic TEST_HOST. App extensions embed by default because the dependency sits on an application target. The `$(TeamIdentifierPrefix)pass.…` value format and the `$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).Class` principal-class pattern are common practice but I couldn't verify them in this research; confirm both by enabling the capability in Xcode once and diffing the result. Capabilities must also be enabled on the App IDs in the developer portal.

pitfalls: The task's 'iOS 26 / Xcode 26' baseline is out of date: Apple docs and the Xcode support page show Xcode 27, iOS 27 SDK and Swift 6.4 as current (27.1 RC and 27.2 beta are already listed). Docs carry iOS 27-only symbols such as `PKPassLibrary.addPasses(data:)` and `PKAddPassesViewController(passesData:)`, so guard them.

Raw bytes: `payloadStringValue` / `payloadString` can be nil or lossy for binary codes such as UIC 918.3 Aztec. `CIBarcodeDescriptor.errorCorrectedPayload` is NOT the decoded payload: it is codewords (Aztec includes stuffed bits, PDF417 uses 16-bit codewords). Use `payloadData` (iOS 17+) only.

Naming differs between APIs: VN `payloadStringValue` vs Swift `payloadString`; `coalesceCompositeSymbologies` (VN and RecognizeDocumentsRequest options) vs `coalescesCompositeSymbologies` (DetectBarcodesRequest); `automaticallyDetectsLanguage`/`usesLanguageCorrection` (RecognizeTextRequest) vs `automaticallyDetectLanguage`/`useLanguageCorrection` (RecognizeDocumentsRequest). Swift `BarcodeObservation` has no `barcodeDescriptor`.

Deprecated APIs to avoid: `VNDetectBarcodesRequest.supportedSymbologies` (class var, since iOS 15; use the throwing instance method), `VNDetectBarcodesRequestRevision1` and `Revision2` (Revision2 deprecated in iOS 18), `VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision1`/`Revision2`, the capitalized `VNBarcodeSymbology` constants (`.QR`, `.Aztec`, `.PDF417`, …), `PKPass.relevantDate` (use `relevantDates`), and `PKPass.paymentPass`.

With `SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY` (NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault) plus MainActor default isolation, any unannotated `async` helper runs on the caller's actor, often the main thread. PDF rasterization and VN* `perform` are synchronous and CPU-heavy, so mark them `@concurrent`.

`VNImageRequestHandler`, `VNRequest`, `VNBarcodeObservation`, `RecognizedItem`, `PKPass` and `PKPassLibrary` are not Sendable. Don't keep them in actors or `Task.detached` closures; extract Data and Strings first. `PKPassLibrary` is documented as not thread-safe.
`DataScannerViewController` and its delegate are `@MainActor`. Its availability properties are `@MainActor class var`s, so reading them from a nonisolated context fails to compile under Swift 6.

`isSupported` only reflects hardware (A12+, false on visionOS); `isAvailable` reflects camera permission and restrictions. Check both. The Simulator has no camera, so expect it to be unsupported there (not explicitly documented) and test on a real device.

Wallet can't render every symbology Vision decodes. iOS 27 added Code39, Codabar, EAN13 and I2of5 to QR, PDF417, Aztec and Code128, but Data Matrix, EAN-8, UPC-E, ITF-14, Code 93, GS1 DataBar, microQR and microPDF417 aren't supported. On iOS 26 devices EAN-13 can't render natively, which requires the iOS 27 fallback array. A POS scanner may reject a re-encoded symbology (for example EAN-13 shown as Code128 or QR).

`PKPassLibrary.isPassLibraryAvailable()` does not mean passes can be added; use `PKAddPassesViewController.canAddPasses()`. `passes()` and `replacePass(with:)` silently return only entitled passes or false without the Wallet entitlement. `addPasses` can return `.shouldReviewPasses`, and then you MUST present `PKAddPassesViewController`.

Share extensions can't use App Attest (`generateKey` fails) and can't open their containing app (`NSExtensionContext.open` works only for Today and iMessage). Any App Store build whose extension contains `TRUEPREDICATE` is rejected.

App Attest keys don't survive reinstall, device migration or backup restore, and `isSupported` is false on Macs, including iOS apps on Apple silicon. The server must not hard-fail those clients. Apple asks apps with millions of DAU to ramp up `attestKey` usage gradually.

`.fileImporter` URLs are security-scoped, so reading without `startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()` fails. `PDFDocument.page(at:)` raises (an Objective-C exception, which crashes) when the index is out of bounds.

Photo orientation: images from PhotosPicker or the camera carry EXIF orientation. Pass the correct `CGImagePropertyOrientation` to `ImageRequestHandler` or `perform(on:orientation:)`, or rotated or small codes may fail to decode.

SwiftData across processes: if both the extension and the app open one store in the App Group container, you take on cross-process write coordination. A file inbox avoids that. Don't pass `@Model` instances across actors (ModelContext isn't Sendable), even though the current SDK's macro declaration lists Sendable; use `PersistentIdentifier`.

XcodeGen doesn't apply Xcode's new-project template defaults (such as MainActor isolation) and has no capability abstraction. Its `projectFormat` enum stops at `xcode16_3`. Entitlements in project.yml must match the App ID capabilities in the developer portal, or automatic signing fails.
PhotosPicker's SwiftUI `Image` Transferable supports only PNG and JPEG; HEIC loses data. Load `Data.self` instead.
open_questions: Does `payloadData` return the exact decoded application bytes for binary Aztec codes (UIC 918.3 / DB tickets, which reportedly start with ASCII '#UT'), including ECI and byte-mode segments? Apple documents it only as 'raw data representation of the barcode's payload'. Test on a device with real DB, ÖBB and SBB tickets and compare against a reference decoder such as ZXing.

Is a scan from a PDF render or screenshot reliable enough for dense Aztec and PDF417 codes compared with live scanning? Pick the render DPI and pixel cap from device tests on low-memory devices (iPhone SE 2nd gen, iPhone 11). Also measure the Share Extension's memory ceiling, which isn't documented.

Which encoding should the backend use for binary payloads in `barcodes[].message` (ISO-8859-1 1:1 mapping vs others), and does Wallet re-render them byte-identically for Aztec, PDF417 and QR? This belongs to the pass-format research but decides what the client sends.

Exact Info.plist and entitlement value formats generated by Xcode 27 for the Wallet capability (`$(TeamIdentifierPrefix)pass.…`) and for the Share extension principal class. Enable each once in Xcode and diff the result to confirm the project.yml values.

Product and legal question: App Review position on an app that re-issues third-party tickets and loyalty cards as passes signed under our own Pass Type ID (guidelines 5.2 intellectual property and 4.1 copycats). PDF417: 16-bit codewords 0…928, where the first codeword is a count that includes itself and padding. DataMatrix: 'de-interleaved bits ... at the end of Step 1: Data encodation'. The property list is incomplete: CIDataMatrixCodeDescriptor also has 'eccVersion: CIDataMatrixCodeDescriptor.ECCVersion'. Per class: QR has symbolVersion, maskPattern and errorCorrectionLevel; Aztec has isCompact, layerCount and dataCodewordCount; PDF417 has isCompact, rowCount and columnCount; DataMatrix has rowCount, columnCount and eccVersion.

missing_important_facts: Possible blocker – App Review Guideline 1.5 (guidelines last updated June 8, 2026): 'ensure that Wallet passes include valid contact information from the issuer and are signed with a dedicated certificate assigned to the brand or trademark owner of the pass.' QRCode2Wallet would sign passes for third parties (Deutsche Bahn, airlines, gyms, retailers) with its own Pass Type ID. Guideline 3.2.1(iv) adds: 'Wallet passes can be used to make or receive payments, transmit offers, or offer identification (such as movie tickets, coupons, and VIP credentials). Other uses may result in the rejection of the app and the revocation of Wallet credentials.' Guideline 5.2.1 forbids using third-party trademarks without permission. Design impact: default to neutral, user-authored passes (no copied third-party logos or brand names; organizationName and contact info refer to QRCode2Wallet and the user), disclose clearly that the pass is not from the issuer, and get an App Review or legal opinion before building the backend. Source: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/

Wallet barcode formats changed in iOS 27. pass.json 'format' now allows PKBarcodeFormatQR, PDF417, Aztec, Code128, Code39, Codabar, EAN13 and I2of5. Before iOS 27 only QR, PDF417, Aztec and Code128 render. Also new in iOS 27: the 'barcodes' array can hold several barcodes as fallbacks ('if you provide EAN 13 and QR formats ... the EAN 13 barcode renders on devices using iOS 27 and later and the QR code renders for devices using pre iOS 27'). Wallet cannot reproduce DataMatrix, EAN-8, UPC-E, Code 93, ITF-14, GS1 DataBar, MicroQR or MicroPDF417 scans in their original symbology, so the app must warn users that a till or turnstile scanner may not accept a substitute. For a deployment target of iOS 26, EAN-13 loyalty cards need a fallback barcode entry. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/walletpasses/pass/barcodes-data.dictionary

The researcher's persistence recommendation rests on a wrong assumption. SwiftData ModelConfiguration defaults to 'groupContainer: ModelConfiguration.GroupContainer = .automatic', which 'Tells SwiftData to use the app's primary group container as the root location for the persistent storage.' Because the app has the App Groups entitlement (for the share extension), the 'default store' will be created inside the App Group container. To keep it private, pass 'groupContainer: .none' explicitly, and decide this before the first release, because moving the store later needs a migration. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftdata/modelconfiguration/init(_:schema:isstoredinmemoryonly:allowssave:groupcontainer:cloudkitdatabase:)

New PassKit APIs in iOS 27 (put behind if #available(iOS 27, *)): PKPassLibrary.addPasses(data: [Data]) async -> PKPassLibraryAddPassesStatus, addPasses(fromArchiveData:) and addPasses(fromArchiveAt:) for .pkpasses bundles, and PKAddPassesViewController init?(passesData:), init?(passesArchiveData:) and init?(passesArchiveAt:). These add passes straight from downloaded bytes without building a PKPass first. New in iOS 26: PKPassLibrary.Capability.backgroundAddPasses (currently the only capability), requestAuthorization(for:) async -> AuthorizationStatus and authorizationStatus(for:). If the user grants backgroundAddPasses, addPasses adds silently. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/passkit/pkpasslibrary/addpasses(data:completion:) , https://developer.apple.com/documentation/passkit/pkpasslibrary/capability

'PKPassLibrary isn't thread-safe. Use instances of this class only on a single thread.' Keep it MainActor-confined. containsPass(_:) works without entitlements. passes() returns only passes the app is entitled to. replacePass(with:) fails unless a pass with the same passTypeIdentifier and serialNumber already exists. The pass-type-identifiers entitlement doc documents '$(TeamIdentifierPrefix)*' (all of the team's passes), which supports the '$(TeamIdentifierPrefix)pass.…' value format. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/passkit/pkpasslibrary , https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/entitlements/com.apple.developer.pass-type-identifiers

(a) Apps built with the 27.0 SDK must include a launch screen key (UILaunchStoryboardName, UILaunchStoryboards, UILaunchScreen or UILaunchScreens) 'or are rejected when the App Store begins accepting apps built with the 27.0 SDK'. The iOS 27 release notes support the @concurrent recommendation. SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY enables DisableOutwardActorInference, GlobalActorIsolatedTypesUsability, InferIsolatedConformances, InferSendableFromCaptures and NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault. App Attest details confirmed for the recommendation. 'The generateKey(completionHandler:) method fails when you call it from an app extension, regardless of the value of isSupported.' isSupported is false on Mac, including iOS apps on Apple silicon. Keys 'don't survive app reinstallation, device migration, or restoration of a device from a backup'. On serverUnavailable, 'try attestation again later with the same key'. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/dcappattestservice/issupported , https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/establishing-your-app-s-integrity , https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/entitlements/com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment
